quotes.text: in 1913, the Italian painter and forward-thinker Luigi Russolo proclaimed intentionally-created noise to be the concert music of the future.
Russolo developed an 'Orchestra of Future Noise Intoners' or 'Intonarumori,' first unveiled at Milan's Futurist headquarters, the Casa Rossa in Milan, on August 11, 1913.
Russolo developed a new notation system for the Intonarumori — the first example of a 'graphic score' in the twentieth century.

The boxes used different mechanisms inside to produce these effects. Some of the sounds were generated by a wheel touching a string attached to a drum — like a hurdy-gurdy. Some instruments featured a handle on top that varied the string tension.
